Commentary.Commentary: That's all we have from this match. The second semi-final between Australia Women and New Zealand Women is coming up shortly. The action will start at 10.30 pm IST (5 pm GMT) but you can join us in advance for the build-up. See you then!

Harmanpreet Kaur, the captain of India Women, says that she needed to be fired up in the middle and remain involved in the game. Praises Smriti Mandhana for her knock and mentions that whoever is performing can keep on scoring the runs. On Shafali's bowling, Kaur replies that she is very confident about her skills and enjoys her bowling. Shares that they will watch the second semi-final and try to learn and plan accordingly.

Smriti Mandhana, the top scorer for India Women, comes up for a chat. She says that she was hoping to get over the line in this tense game. Admits that the fielding was not up to the mark. Tells that Deepti Sharma's overs in the middle were important and also praises Sneh Rana for handling the pressure. Regarding her form, Smriti Mandhana replies that she has been batting well and is happy to find the touch. She hopes to repeat the same in the final also.

Earlier, it was an excellent batting show by India Women, powered by Smriti Mandhana's fabulous knock. They did stutter a bit in the middle phase but then managed to finish strongly with a challenging total on the board with the help of Jemimah Rodrigues' innings.

England Women will be hurting! They had this game in their grasp but it slipped away towards the end. 48 runs were needed off 30 balls with 7 wickets in hand but the home team failed to get the final push and suffered a heartbreaking loss. The start from them was brilliant and despite losing wickets, England Women were in control of the required rate. Credit to India Women for hanging in there and creating opportunities. They seized the initiative when it mattered the most and then managed to close the game in their favour.

Revenge is a dish best served cold - India Women have done it, they have avenged their loss in the 2017 World Cup final and in the 2018 T20 World Cup semi-final by knocking out the home team, England Women from the gold medal race. The Indian players are ecstatic. What a win for them!

SIX! But that won't be enough! England Women are knocked out. Floated delivery, full and around off, Sophie Ecclestone advances down the track and powers it over long on. India Women win by 4 runs and are in the final!
India have secured a place in the final, if there is no drama on the final ball. Fullish and on middle, knocked down to long on for just a single.
Put down! Fuller and around middle, Sophie lofts it without much timing to long on where Harleen Deol (sub) puts down a straightforward catch. A single is taken.
Sophie Ecclestone is the new batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Flighted and full, around middle, Katherine Brunt plays a mistimed aerial shot, from the bottom half of her bat and it is a simple catch for Harmanpreet Kaur at mid off. Big blow to England.
Commentary.Howout: c Harmanpreet Kaur b Sneh Rana

Commentary.Commentary: Full toss around off, Maia walks forward and pushes it to mid off for a quick run. 13 needed off 4 balls.

Stumping appeal! Sneh Rana fires it full and wide outside off, Maia Bouchier flashes at it but misses. Taniya Bhatia takes the bails off. The replays find that Maia Bouchier's back leg is just inside the crease.
Slow over-rate means that India Women will have to put one extra fielder inside the ring. Sneh Rana to bowl...
Short in length and outside off, Brunt tries to pull but misses. 14 needed off 6 balls.
Katherine Brunt is the new batter.

OUT! SCIVER IS RUN OUT! 15 needed off 7 balls. Slower one, full and around middle, Sciver heaves it to deep mid-wicket for a run. Natalie Sciver turns for the second run and tries to get in with a full-length dive but before that Smriti Mandhana has fired in an accurate throw from the deep and Taniya Bhatia breaks the stumps. The replays confirm the departure of the English skipper.
Appeal for a run out...
FOUR LEG BYES! Fortunate boundary but Englan Women will take it. Fuller in length, around leg, Natalie Sciver fails to flick and it goes off her pads to the fine leg fence.
SIX! Dispatched! This is what England Women need. The crowd comes back to life. Short again, around off, Natalie Sciver rocks back and hammers it in front of square leg for a biggie.
Off pace again, short and on middle, Maia steps back and punches it to wide long off for one. 25 needed off 10 balls.
Slower one, short and on off, Sciver pulls it to deep square leg but gets only a run. Singles won't do it for England Women.
Pooja Vastrakar to bowl the 19th over.
Too full and around off, Sciver digs it out towards long on and picks up a run. 27 needed off 12 balls, a big over coming up.

Shout for an lbw, but the umpire shakes her head. Quicker one, full and outside off, Natalie Sciver shuffles across and tries to sweep but misses. She is rapped on the pads, they appeal but the umpire turns it down. Harmanpreet Kaur has a word with her players and takes the DRS. UltraEdge shows a slight inside edge. India Women are now left with no reviews.
Short in length and wide outside off, Maia Bouchier reaches out and thumps it to deep cover for one.
Walks down the track and knocks it down to long on for a single.
Maia Bouchier is the new batter in.

OUT! RUN OUT! The pressure was building and it resulted in a wicket. Flighted delivery, around off, Amy drives it towards extra cover and sets off for a non-existent single. Radha Yadav immediately releases the ball towards the bowler and Sneh Rana does the rest. Amy Jones is not even in the frame. 30 needed off 16 balls.
Swing and a miss! Loopy delivery, full and outside off, Amy Jones tries to slog-sweep but misses.
Sneh Rana comes into the attack now.
Short and wide outside off, punched in front of square on the off side for one. 30 needed off 18 balls. This is going down to the wire.
Around leg, it's tickled behind square leg for a single.
Tossed up around off, Natalie Sciver tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Walks down the track but drives it straight to mid off.
Full and outside off, driven to deep cover for one.
Flatter and shorter outside off, pulled with a reverse bat but straight to backward point.
Risky third. Floated and full, outside off, Jones walks across the stumps and sweeps it behind square leg. She scampers back for the third run and completes it with a dive. The 50-run stand comes up.
FOUR! Put away! Short in length and around off, Amy plays the reverse-batted shot and pulls it from the toe-end of her bat past backward point for a boundary.

FOUR! A vital boundary for England Women. Loopy delivery, full and outside off, Amy Jones cracks it square of the wicket on the off side. The point fielder dives in vain, the deep cover fielder dives as well but again in vain.
Full and around off, Jones drives it to covers where the fielder fumbles and concedes two runs.
Stays back and punches it through covers for a single.
Risky. Amy Jones walks across the stumps and scoops it from the upper half of her bat. It brushes the hands of the keeper and deflects behind. They cross.
Last 5 overs left, 48 needed off 30 balls.
Goes fuller and on off, Amy Jones flicks it towards mid-wicket for one. Good over for India Women. Just 4 runs off it.
Tossed up outside off, Amy Jones plays a reverse sweep towards backward point but finds the fielder.
Serves it outside off, Amy Jones looks to play at it but misses.
This one lands fuller and on leg, Natalie Sciver flicks it towards short fine leg for a single.
Outside off this time, Amy Jones cuts it towards deep point for a single.
Full toss on middle, Natalie Sciver pulls it towards backward square leg for one.
Deepti Sharma is back into the attack. 1 for 11 in her two overs so far.
Bowls it outside off, Natalie Sciver cuts it towards deep cover for one more. 9 from the over for England Women. 52 needed off 36 balls.
Tossed up, around off, Amy Jones drives it to extra cover for one more.
Outside off again, Natalie Sciver punches it towards covers.
Fuller and on off, Amy Jones drives it to extra cover for a single.
Mid off drops back.
FOUR! Up and over the infield. Flighted delivery outside off, fuller in length, Amy Jones decides to go aerial and sends it flying behind mid off for a boundary.
Tossed up on off, Natalie Sciver flicks it towards long on for one.
Another one outside off, this is played towards deep point for one more.
Outside off and fuller, Amy Jones guides it to covers for one.
Fuller and on off, Natalie Sciver drives it straight towards the bowler who just manages to get her hand on it. They take a quick single.
On a length and just outside off, slower too, Natalie Sciver looks to drive it but misses.
FOUR! 100 comes up! Short in length and wide outside off, Natalie Sciver whacks it through the gap at cover-point for a boundary.
Renuka Singh serves it around off, Natalie Sciver eases it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Renuka Singh is back on.
Bowls it on leg this time, Natalie Sciver sweeps it towards backward square leg for one.
Fuller and outside off, Natalie Sciver steers it towards backward point.
Tossed up, around middle and leg, Amy Jones flicks it towards backward square leg for one.

Shout for an lbw, not given! An arm ball, landing around middle and skidding down, Amy Jones fails to sweep and is hit on the pads. They appeal but nothing from the umpire. India Women review the decision but the Ball Tracking finds the impact to be with the umpire's call and it's missing the stumps after that. India have one review left now.
Tossed up, around middle and leg, Natalie Sciver sweeps it to backward square leg for one.
Fuller and on middle, Natalie Sciver defends it solidly.
Touch fuller and on off, Amy Jones drives it towards the deep cover for a couple of runs.
Goes fuller and down the leg side, Natalie Sciver nudges it towards mid-wicket for one.
Slower and outside off, this is cut towards point.
On off and fuller, Amy Jones eases it towards cover-point for one more.
Goes fuller, this is flicked towards short fine leg for one.
Two wides! Bowls it outside leg, Amy Jones looks to flick it but misses. The keeper fumbles to collect it. They cross. Wide called.
Fuller and on off, Natalie Sciver drives it to covers for one.
Width outside off, cut to deep point for a single. 79 needed at the halfway mark.
Swing and a miss and it beats the stumps by a whisker. Slower one, around off, Natalie Sciver goes hard at it but fails to connect. It shaves past the stumps.
Shorter and outside off, this is guided towards covers.
Good-length delivery on the pads, Jones looks to flick this but the ball gets off the pads towards short cover. They cross for a leg bye. A direct hit at the bowler's end could have been close.

Back of a length again, Amy Jones pulls it towards deep square leg. Two fielders converge, Meghna Singh from fine leg and Harleen (sub) from deep square leg. The former pulls out very late and seems to have hurt her left leg. Two runs taken.
Slightly shorter on middle, Natalie Sciver pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for one.
Amy Jones is the new batter.

OUT! Drags it on! Rana serves it a touch short and outside off, once again Danni Wyatt walks across the stumps to attempt for the paddle sweep but gets too close to the line of the delivery. She ends up getting an inside edge and the ball deflects onto the stumps. Wyatt is very disappointed on her way back. 84 needed off 66 balls.
FOUR! Danni Wyatt continues to flourish. Flighted delivery, full and around off, Danni Wyatt goes down and across and scoops it down to fine leg for a boundary.
Fuller one around middle and leg, Natalie Sciver flicks it towards mid-wicket where Smriti Mandhana makes a good diving stop to her right. They cross.
Fuller in length, Natalie Sciver drives it but finds the fielder at covers.
A low full toss, Natalie Sciver plays it straight towards the mid off fielder.
FOUR! Excellent use of the feet! Loopy delivery, landing full and around off, Sciver dances down the track and lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
Short of a length, Natalie Sciver pulls it towards fine leg for one.
On a length and on leg, Natalie Sciver flicks it towards mid-wicket for a brace.
Shorter one around middle, Danni Wyatt pulls it but gets a top edge. The ball goes in the air and lands short of the fielder at fine leg. They cross.
Short and on off, Natalie Sciver pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Goes outside off this time, Danni Wyatt eases it towards point and takes a single.
Serves it on a length and down the leg side, Natalie Sciver flicks it towards backward square leg for one.
Pooja Vastrakar comes into the attack.
Flighted up on off, Danni Wyatt cuts it towards the fielder at point. End of a successful over for India Women.
Fuller and around off, Natalie Sciver hits it to long on for one.
Outside off again, Natalie Sciver eases it to the off side. She wants a single but Danni Wyatt sends her back.
Tossed up, outside off, Danni Wyatt drives it towards deep cover for one.
Natalie Sciver walks in next. 102 needed off 82 balls.

OUT! RUN OUT! Floated delivery, full and around off, Alice Capsey tries for an inside-out shot over covers but ends up slicing it towards point. They cross for a run and Alice turns blind for the second run. Her partner never responded. Alice Capsey then realizes that the throw is already in the keeper's gloves. She tries to scoot back as Taniya Bhatia throws the ball to the bowler who breaks the stumps. It's referred upstairs. The replays show that Alice Capsey tries to slide her bat in but it's the back side of the bat on the inside. It means that nothing is grounded inside the crease as we can see the shadow. India Women were unaware of that and it comes as a sweet surprise for them to see OUT flash on the screen.
Appeal for a run out...
FOUR! Brave shot! Flighted and around off, Alice Capsey brings out the reverse sweep and nails it wide of short third man for a boundary.
Sneh Rana to bowl after the Powerplay.

Is that dropped? Sounded like an edge. Singh serves it full and outside off, slower in pace, Danni Wyatt tries to drive but fails to middle her shot. There appears to be an under edge but Taniya Bhatia fails to gather the ball. At the end of the Powerplay, England Women are 58 for 1.
FOUR! Placed to perfection! Short in length and wide outside off, Danni Wyatt sits back and guides it nice and late through the gap between short third man and backward point.
Fails to put away a freebie. Danni Wyatt fetches a full toss from outside off and heaves it over mid-wicket for a couple.
A length ball again, on off, it's forced from the back foot to sweeper cover for a single.
Around off, on a length, Danni taps it down to cover-point and steals a run.
Delivers it short and outside off, Alice Capsey stays back and hits it to sweeper cover for a run. 50 up!
Renuka Singh comes back into the attack.
A long hop again, outside off, Wyatt cuts but finds the point fielder. A poor over but it goes for only 7 runs.
Loopy and full, just inside the tramline outside off, the batter leaves thinking it to be a wide. Not given.
Flatter through the air, short and wide, Alice Capsey throws her bat at it and bottom-edges it past short third man. They cross.
Short again outside off, Danni Wyatt chops it down to point and crosses.
Short and wide outside off, Capsey cuts it to short third man where the fielder fumbles and concedes a run.
FOUR! Fine leg up and it's a safe shot. Loopy and full, around middle and off, Alice Capsey walks across and sweeps it past short fine leg for a boundary.
FOUR! Delicate from Danni this time. A length ball, sliding down the leg side, Danni Wyatt plays late and tickles it fine down the leg side for a boundary. 123 needed off 96 balls.
Mid-wicket drops back.
FOUR! Boom! A poor delivery with a 7-2 field. No protection in the deep on the leg side. Fuller in length, around middle, Danni Wyatt heaves it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Around off, on a length, Danni plays it down to point and looks for a run. She is sent back.
Danni goes in front of square this time. Full and outside off, it's stroked through cover-point for a couple of runs.
FOUR! That's her area, Danni loves it square. Width there outside off, shaping away, Danni Wyatt hammers it through backward point for a boundary.
Full in length and around off, Danni Wyatt tries to tap and run but is sent back as the point fielder quickly gets to the ball.
Loopy and full, around off, Alice Capsey drives it back and Deepti Sharma parries it to mid off. Seems to have hurt her fingers. Nonetheless, a successful over from her.
Alice Capsey is the new batter in.

OUT! GIVEN LBW! Deepti Sharma finally gets her line and length right and immediately strikes. Flighted and full, around off and turning in a hint, Sophia Dunkley goes down on one knee to sweep but misses the ball. She is rapped on the front pad, they appeal and the finger goes up. Sophia Dunkley has a word with her partner regarding the usage of the DRS but is advised against it.
Again the length is short and it's outside off, Danni Wyatt cuts from the back foot and it races away to deep point. They take one.
Slightly short and around off, Sophia pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Sharma sees the batter coming down the track and shortens her length. Delivers it outside off and Wyatt cuts it to deep cover for a run.
Flighted delivery, around off, Dunkley takes it on the full and forces it down to long on for a run.
Deepti Sharma comes into the attack.
Shaping away from a length outside off, Danni pushes at it and misses. Three good balls to close the over.
Identical to the last delivery, Danni Wyatt defends it with a straight bat.
Fuller in length, on middle and shaping away, Danni Wyatt defends it to the off side.
The Indian physio has come out to perform the mandatory concussion check on Taniya Bhatia. All is good and the game resumes.

On a length and outside off, Sophia Dunkley swings her bat at it but fails to connect. Taniya Bhatia fails to gather the ball and is hit on the helmet. The ball deflects on the leg side and they cross for a bye.
FOUR! Lovely shot! A low full toss, around off, Sophia Dunkley kneels down and plays a drop-kick over mid-wicket for a boundary.

FOUR! The second over also begins with a boundary down the ground. Too full in length and outside off, Sophia Dunkley drives it from the bottom half of his bat and it races away past the bowler. Harmanpreet Kaur tries to chase from mid off but fails to get it back.
Meghna Singh to bowl from the other end.
Length and on off, defended to the off side. 15 from the first over!

FOUR! Beautifully placed! A touch short in length, around off and shaping in, Danni Wyatt stays back and plays at it very late, almost off the keeper's gloves. She manages to thread the gap between slip and backward point and it races away to the fence.
Movement in the air and off the pitch. A length ball, shaping in, Danni defends it from the back foot.
On a length and around off, Dunkley heaves it off the inner half to deep mid-wicket. One run is taken.
Wide! Slightly short and down the leg side, Sophia tries to flick but misses.
Fuller this time, around off, Sophia Dunkley drives it off the front foot to mid off.
FOUR! Dunkley takes full advantage of the Free Hit! Shortish delivery, around middle, Sophia Dunkley sits on the back foot and heaves it over wide mid on for a boundary.

FOUR! What a way to start! A full toss on off, Dunkley shows the full face of the bat and caresses it past the diving mid off fielder for a boundary. It's a no ball as well for overstepping. Free Hit coming...
